Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

leader noun

also leaders, chief, head of a group, leading man, ringleader, team leader, political leader

classical

Liv. 2.13.6: dux agminis virginum
Cic. de Or. 3.63: dux regendae cīvitātis (Lewis & Short)

dux, ducis m./f.

noun, third declension, masculine or feminine

a leader, a guide; in war, a commander

The general word for whoever leads a group, a party or an army, and feminine as well: dux fēmina factī (Verg. A. 1.364, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • prīnceps, prīncipis m. — the leading man; in the plural, the leaders of a people

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.30.1: tōtīus ferē Galliae lēgātī, prīncipēs cīvitātum; Traupman 338: leader; Traupman 290; Traupman 338

    Under the emperors, the emperor’s own title, chosen by Augustus.

  • rēctor, rēctōris m. — one who steers: the leader of a state

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.52: rēctor et gubernātor cīvitātis (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. leader, ruler

    From the helmsman (Lewis & Short); Morgan–Owens has it for the leader of a nation.

  • ductor, ductōris m. — a leader, a commander

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 1.28 (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 2.14 (Lewis & Short)

    Classical prose has it (Cicero, Livy), but it is above all a favourite word of Vergil’s, who uses it more than twenty times (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus … frūstrāta custōdēs, dux agminis virginum inter tēla hostium Tiberim trānāvit

    Cloelia, a girl who was one of the hostages, slipped past her guards and, at the head of a band of girls, swam the Tiber under the enemy’s spearsLiv. 2.13.6

See also president, group, team, government, rule.

SourcesLewis & Short: dux · Lewis & Short: princeps · Lewis & Short: rector · Lewis & Short: ductor

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: leader, ruler, person who governs.
